summary: Sanit Sinak works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Mahamakut Buddhist University, Silpakorn University, and Ramkhamhaeng University, and served as an instructor at Mahamakut Buddhist University in 2014.

Sanjay Shakya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He earned a master's degree from Tribhuvan University (2008–2009) and became an assistant professor at Lumbini Buddhist University in 2024.

Historian Sanjay Subrahmanyam studied at St. Stephen's College, the Delhi School of Economics, and the University of Delhi. He held positions at Oxford, the EHESS, UCLA—where he became Distinguished Professor in 2014—and the Collège de France (2013–2021).
Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under M. K. Ganguli and traditional teacher A. P. Lama.

Sanjukta Gupta works in Indology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Calcutta, Visva-Bharati University, and Utrecht University under Jan Gonda, and held posts at Jadavpur, Utrecht, and Oxford, as well as Visva-Bharati and Calcutta.

Sanjukta Poddar specializes in Indology and history and archaeology. She earned an MA and PhD at the University of Chicago (2015–2022), where she was a postdoctoral teaching fellow in 2022, before joining Leiden University as assistant professor in 2023.

Sanne Dokter-Mersch works in Indology and religious studies. She completed her PhD at Leiden University (~2015–2021) under Peter C. Bisschop and Yuko Yokochi, and served as a postdoctoral researcher there in 2022.

Santanu Sarkar works in Indology. He studied at North Bengal, Cooch Behar Panchanan Barma, and Burdwan universities, and conducted PhD research at IIT Kharagpur (2020–2026), becoming an assistant professor at the University of Engineering & Management in 2026.

Sao Htun Hmat Win was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard University and under Bhaddanta Narada. He taught at the University of Rangoon, headed research at the International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies, and advised Myanmar's Ministry of Religious Affairs.

Sara Frumento works in Indology and history and archaeology. She studied for a DPhil in Area Studies (South Asia) at Wolfson College, University of Oxford, and held a post at the University of Oxford.

Sara Grant was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She studied at Oxford, under Richard De Smet, and earned a PhD at the University of Mumbai, later holding posts at Sophia College, Jnana-Deepa Vidyapeeth, and Christa Prema Seva Ashram.

Sara L. McClintock works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. She studied at Columbia, CIHTS, Lausanne, and Harvard (PhD, 2002) under Tom Tillemans, later teaching at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and Emory University.

Sarah Aoife Richardson specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Toronto in 2016 under Jenny Purtle, having also studied under John C. and Susan L. Huntington, among others.

Sarah Cymbal specializes in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University of Culture and Arts and the Russian-Armenian University, where she held a post, and directed the Centre for the study of Silk Road art.

Sarah E. Fraser is a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Michigan and Kobe University, and held appointments at Northwestern University from 1996 and the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2000.

Sarah H. Jacoby specializes in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale University and completed her PhD at the University of Virginia in 2007, later holding posts at Columbia University and Northwestern University.

Sarah Harding works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche and Lama Tenpa, taught at Naropa University (~1992–2018), and served as a fellow at the Tsadra Foundation from ~2000.

Sarah J. Horton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein and served as an assistant professor at Macalester College (attested 2006).
Sarah Merkle-Schneider is an Indology scholar who completed an M.A. at the University of Tübingen and held an affiliated post there in 2026.

Sarah Shaw is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Lance S. Cousins. She has been affiliated with Oxford's Faculty of Oriental Studies, Wolfson College, and the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies.
